domain: health-system operations - NHS emergency care four-hour performance prediction (UK public-service performance panel)
prediction_question: For an NHS England provider operating a consultant-led (Type 1) A&E department, will the percentage of its Type 1 attendances admitted, transferred or discharged within 4 hours of arrival decline in month M+1 relative to month M, given that provider's monthly A&E series (attendances by department type and booked-appointment status, over-4-hour counts, waits from decision-to-admit, emergency admissions) for all months through M, plus calendar month? A relative month-over-month change is used instead of a fixed standard threshold because the fixed thresholds measured near-uniform positive rates in recent years (see measurements).
prediction_time: End of month M, when month M's monthly CSV is published (measured: the September 2026 monthly CSV was already downloadable on 2026-10-21, i.e. a ~3 week publication lag). Every feature is derived from provider months <= M; the label is month M+1's within-4-hour rate versus month M's, and month M+1's row is published about a month after the prediction is made.
target_definition: Binary, computed from the source row of month M+1: within4h_rate(M+1) < within4h_rate(M), where within4h_rate(Y) = 1 - Attendances over 4hrs Type 1 / A&E attendances Type 1 for the provider in month Y. Unit: proportion of Type 1 attendances within 4 hours. Label source columns: month M+1's 'A&E attendances Type 1' and 'Attendances over 4hrs Type 1' (recorded in label_source_columns; excluded from shipped columns). Volume gate: provider-month excluded unless Type 1 attendances >= 100 in both M and M+1 (measured: leaves 124 providers with >= 24 such months).

construction_script: candidates/nhs-ae-four-hour-decline/source/build.py (stdlib only; --source-dir reads a staged/predownloaded copy of the 102 monthly CSVs, the default HTTP path enumerates the year pages - blocked from datacenter IPs, see measurements.publisher_cdn_datacenter_block; --smoke relaxes acceptance for bounded exercises)
split_strategy: Temporal, on the target month M+1, windows recomputed 2026-10-21 on the corrected panel (102 months 2018-04..2026-09, 134 providers; see probe_defect_correction_2026_10_21): train targets 2019-01..2022-12 = 6,116 provider-months (3,285 positives, 53.7%); eval targets 2023-01..2024-12 = 2,937 (1,478 positives, 50.3%); holdout targets 2025-01..2026-09 = 2,538 (1,233 positives, 48.6%). Both classes present in every window. Positives cluster within providers (a declining provider tends to keep declining), so the conservative independent-unit count is the distinct positive providers per window: 133 (train) / 124 (eval) / 121 (holdout) of 134 providers. Features for the earliest train rows draw on 2018-04..2018-12 history. Rows are keyed (Org Code, target month) - shipped as the composite row_id '<ORG>-<YYYY-MM>'; providers with <100 Type 1 attendances in either month are excluded by the volume gate.

measurements.panel_2026_10_21: Corrected 2026-10-21 (see probe_defect_correction_2026_10_21): 102 monthly CSVs 2018-04..2026-09 (every month the year pages carry), 21,649 rows read, 101 non-monthly Period rows (TOTAL artefacts, excluded), 21,548 (org, month) keys - NO duplicate keys exist across the 102 files (each month is published in exactly one file, so the recorded 'revision dedup' never had anything to dedup; the build still implements prefer-latest-upload). 134 providers with Type 1 attendances >= 100 in >= 24 months -> 12,765 qualifying provider-months; 12,631 consecutive qualifying pairs (1,040 with target months before 2019-01, outside the split windows). The discovery session's recorded panel (20,497 keys / 97 months / 124 providers / 9,071 provider-months) was computed with the two probe defects described in probe_defect_correction_2026_10_21 and is superseded.
measurements.national_within4h_type1_by_year: Corrected 2026-10-21 on the full 102-month panel (volume-gated providers): 2018 83.0%, 2019 78.1%, 2020 82.6%, 2021 72.9%, 2022 62.4%, 2023 59.8%, 2024 58.6%, 2025 60.2%, 2026 YTD 61.0%. The recorded series (2020 85.1%, 2021 73.2%, 2023 60.1%) covered only the months the damaged panel retained (no qualifying month before 2020-04; 2023-07/08/09 dropped). August 2026 national Type 1 within-4h recomputed on the corrected panel: 60.86% vs the publisher commentary's 61.1% - the cross-check still holds (revised-vs-provisional publication states). NAO HC 588 fiscal-year anchors remain consistent within calendar-year offsets.
measurements.label_base_rates_measured: Corrected 2026-10-21 on the full panel: m/m decline label train(2019-01..2022-12 targets) 6,116 rows / 3,285 positives = 53.7%; eval(2023-01..2024-12) 2,937 / 1,478 = 50.3%; holdout(2025-01..2026-09) 2,538 / 1,233 = 48.6% (holdout unchanged - its months were intact in the damaged panel). Fixed-threshold labels RE-COMPUTED on the corrected panel and still REFUSED: within4h < 95% gives train 87.2% / eval 97.5% / holdout 99.9% positive (uniform-class red flag); < 80% gives holdout 95.8%; < 74% gives holdout 90.8%. The refusal conclusion and the base-rate non-stationarity property stand unchanged.
measurements.cost_measured: 102 CSV GETs, 3,115,779 bytes, 1.2 s wall clock on the coordinator (1.9 GiB class host) + 11 year-page GETs (~80 KB each) to enumerate URLs. Full-history extension to 2015-06 requires the cumulative Monthly-AE-Time-Series .xls (440 KB) parsed on a worker (xlrd), or per-month XLS for 2015-16..2017-18.
measurements.revision_policy_measured: Re-measured 2026-10-21 at construction: across the 102 monthly CSVs there are NO duplicate (org, month) keys - each calendar month is published in exactly one file (originals are replaced on the year page by their '...revised...' successor, e.g. April-2020-revised-260421), so the recorded 'keep max Type 1 attendances' dedup never operated on anything. The build still implements prefer-latest-upload (ordered by the revision datestamp in the filename, then revised flag) and reports the dedup count, which measured 0.
measurements.known_event_note: December 2021 (Omicron) moves the national aggregate only slightly (65.6% vs 66.2% in Nov 2021, quick un-deduped national check) - winter pressure shows at provider grain, so it is not a usable national known-event fixture; the publisher-commentary cross-check above anchors the rate computation instead. The m/m-decline label has no external threshold, so the qualification known-event fixture requirement does not apply; seasonal structure (winter declines) is the headroom signal a competent model must capture.
measurements.no_cross_split_entities: org codes repeat across splits by design (same providers tracked over time) - the entity is the provider-month, not the provider; the gate's expected_duplicate_ids must not claim org codes as entity keys, and id columns for the runner are (Org Code, target month).
measurements.probe_defect_correction_2026_10_21: CORRECTION 2026-10-21 (construction session): the discovery panel probe (probe_panel.py) had two defects that silently shrank its panel, and every figure below was recomputed on the corrected load (build.py --source-dir over the same 102 CSVs; script .factory/nhsae_recompute.py, command and output in notes.md). Defect 1: the probe opened files with encoding="utf-8", so the five BOM-prefixed files (July 2019, August 2021, July/August/September 2023) keyed Period as "\ufeffPeriod", d.get("Period") returned "" and five whole months were dropped (probe printed '1,152 non-monthly rows' where the true count is 101 TOTAL rows; 1,051 were BOM-file rows). Defect 2: the probe looked up "A&E attendances Type 1", but the 2018-04..2020-03 files name the column "Number of A&E attendances Type 1", so att1 parsed as 0 for 24 months and no provider-month before 2020-04 ever passed the volume gate - the recorded '97 months' panel in fact had no qualifying month before 2020-04. The corrected build reads utf-8-sig and normalises the 'Number of' prefix: 102 months 2018-04..2026-09 (every month the year pages carry), 21,548 provider-months, 134 providers with >= 24 qualifying months, 12,765 qualifying provider-months.
measurements.schema_evolution_2026_10_21: Measured at construction across all 102 files: 16 data columns 2018-04..2020-07 (the 2018-04..2020-03 files prefix counts with 'Number of'); booked-appointment columns appear from 2020-08 (22 columns); files from 2024-09 carry 28 header fields of which the last six are unnamed/zero padding. Booked-appointment columns are parsed but NOT shipped: they are absent for train feature months 2018-12..2020-07, so their availability would be split-dependent - a prediction-timing defect wearing a feature-list costume. The 12 core columns are published across the whole window and are the only shipped source columns.
measurements.publisher_cdn_datacenter_block: Measured 2026-10-21: www.england.nhs.uk (CloudFront) serves HTTP 202 with an empty body to the Hetzner worker IP (65.21.158.17, from both servers tried), for every year page; the same URLs serve 200/82,127 B with 12 CSV links to the coordinator under three User-Agent variants. Consequence: construction jobs cannot fetch this publisher from a worker; the 102 CSVs are fetched on the coordinator (measured 3.1 MB total) and staged in the private staging repo, and the job consumes them with per-file sha256 verification. The build's default HTTP path remains for reproducing from an unblocked network.
